target: petal PO:0009032 + absent PATO:0000462; floral disc absent (no PO term for the floral disc; nearest is nectary PO:0009035)

target: leaf sheath auricle PO:0020106 + absent PATO:0000462; oral setae = trichome PO:0000282 + absent PATO:0000462 (at the sheath shoulder)

target: leaf sheath auricle PO:0020106 + absent PATO:0000462 (sheath auricles); cilia = trichome PO:0000282 + absent PATO:0000462
fix: In grasses and bamboos (Poaceae, Bambusoideae), 'auricle(s)' is the sheath auricle (PO:0020106), never a stipule. Map 'auricle' to stipule only for dicot leaves described with stipules.
reason: 'auricles and cilia absent' refers to bamboo sheath auricles, not stipules. 'leathery' probably describes the culm sheath, so the stipule: coriaceous record is also wrongly mapped.

target: aerial tuber (bulbil) PO:0004548 + absent PATO:0000462, context: distal leaves/axils

target: ultimate inflorescence branches + sterile PATO:0000956 (flowerless, needle-like); not flower absent for the taxon
fix: '<branches> with no flowers' / 'flowerless branches' means those branches are sterile (PATO:0000956), not that the plant lacks flowers.
reason: In Acroglochin the ultimate inflorescence branches end as sterile needle-like spines; the flowers sit on the lower branches.

target: stage: lenticels absent on young branchlets vs conspicuous on old ones
fix: When 'absent' is followed in the same sentence by a quality qualified by 'when old/young/mature', keep the stage context on both statements and do not assert a plain absence for the taxon.
reason: The 'conspicuous when old' fragment is a stage-qualified clause about the same lenticels, so the two statements describe different ages.

target: no annotation (inflorescence not observed); the infructescence statement stays
fix: 'not seen', 'unknown', 'not known', 'not observed' mean missing data, never absence; produce no statement.
reason: 'Inflorescences not seen' means the specimens lacked flowers. It says nothing about the plant having none.

target: check the source: pappus absent may refer to a particular floret or achene type, or be a typo
fix: Before asserting absence for a taxon, look for a member qualifier (ray/disc, outer/inner, female/bisexual) earlier in the same sentence and attach it.
reason: Ainsliaea normally has a plumose pappus. Without the sentence it is unclear whether the absence is scoped to some florets or is a source error.

target: no annotation (flowers not observed)
fix: 'not seen' / 'unknown' means missing data, never absent.
reason: 'Flowers not seen' only means the specimens were fruiting.

target: position: sterile bracts absent on the peduncle vs floral bracts present in the inflorescence
fix: '<part> ebracteate' restricts the bract absence to that part (here the peduncle); do not assert bract absent for the whole plant.
reason: Orchid peduncles can lack sterile bracts while each flower still has a floral bract, which is the acuminate one.

target: petiole PO:0020038 + length PATO:0000122 0–2.5 cm (petiole sometimes absent / variable)
fix: 'absent to N unit' / '0–N unit' is a length range starting at zero. Read it as a length value with variable presence, not as absence.

target: wing petal PO:0025325 + absent PATO:0000462; keel PO:0025327 + absent PATO:0000462

reason: Amorpha has only the standard; wings and keel are missing. The standard (banner petal PO:0025324) is purple.

target: different parts: the muticous apex and the awned apex belong to different organs (e.g. leaf vs bract/bracteole)

reason: Both statements are about apices of different organs in the same description. 'muticous' (no awn or point) and 'awned' cannot hold for one apex.

target: false (recurrent) veins absent; no PO term (not vascular bundle PO:0005020) — leave unannotated or propose a FLOPO anatomy class
fix: 'false vein(s)' / 'recurrent false veins' are not veins and must not map to vascular bundle; skip or map to a dedicated class.
reason: False veins in Angiopteris are non-vascular strips between the true veins; the true veins are present and obvious.

target: whorl: inner petals absent vs outer petals present (reddish)

target: pistillode PO:0009078 + absent PATO:0000462, context: male flower (PATO:0000384)

target: member: pedicelled spikelet absent vs sessile spikelets present (lowermost barren)

reason: In Apocopis the pedicelled spikelet is often missing while the sessile spikelets are there.

target: leaf lamina PO:0020039 without a collective marginal vein (no PO term); not vascular bundle absent

target: no annotation (capsules not observed)

target: position: leaflike bracts on the upper stem vs heads/branches without bracts

target: spikelet PO:0009051 with trichome PO:0000282 (tubercle-based) absent

target: ray flower PO:0025331: pappus absent; disk flower PO:0025332: pappus present (brownish white)
